 UPI Charges Applies Above Rs 2000 Payment: Will You Get Full Refund After Cancellation?
 Mitali

 UPI Charges on payment above ₹2,000 was scheduled to be introduced from 15th October 2026. However, National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) postponed the implementation due to the festive season but there is no confirmation yet about the revised date.
 UPI MDR Rules for Payments Above ₹2,000
 NPCI has introduced a revised Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on selected merchant transactions. The charges include:
 Transaction Category 
 Proposed MDR 
 Merchant payments (P2M) up to ₹2,000 
 Nil 
 Merchant payments (P2M) above ₹2,000 
 0.40% 
 Payments of ₹75,000 and above 
 Maximum ₹300 
 Railways, fuel, telecom, insurance etc. Above ₹2,000 
 Flat ₹5 
 Mutual funds, securities and stockbroking Above ₹2,000 
 0.02%, capped at ₹300 
 Small Merchants (P2PM Category) Up to ₹1 Lakh per month 
 Nil 
 Explore More in Details - New UPI Rules 2026: Complete Fee Structure for Transactions 
 Who will pay the UPI MDR charges: customers or merchants?
 The proposed MDR will be borne by eligible merchants and not the customers. Merchants cannot charge from customers as a UPI transaction fee.
 Will The Customer Get a Full Refund After Cancelling a UPI Payment?
 Customers are generally expected to receive the full amount paid, subject to the merchant's applicable cancellation and refund terms.
 For example: If a customer purchase a Mobile Phone amounting: ₹50,000
 Applicable MDR at 0.4%: ₹200
 Amount paid by customer: ₹50,000
 Expected customer refund: ₹50,000
 As MDR will be borne by eligible merchants, it should not be deducted from the customer's refund.
 Will Merchants Get the MDR Amount Back?
 This is where the issue becomes complicated.
 If a customer cancels an order after successful payment, the merchant may have to refund the entire purchase amount while absorbing the original MDR.
 The current framework does not clearly explain whether MDR will be reversed in cases of full refunds or partial refunds.
 For businesses dealing with frequent cancellations and product returns, this could increase payment processing costs.
